title: Drawing techniques: how a figure is constructed
reads_with: human-canon.json (landmark names, widths and depths in heads)
how_to_use: Build in this order. Each step is a simple form placed between two canon landmarks, with its cross-section and how many planes it gets. Contour (muscle bulges) comes only after every form is placed, and detail (folds, cloth, armour) only after the planes read. A modeler builds these as primitives first, then lofts the contour over them; a Midjourney prompt asks for the same order of qualities.

sources.loomis: Figure Drawing for All It's Worth (1943): the line of action, the bean-free mannequin frame (ribcage and pelvis blocks on a flexible spine), the 'straights against curves' principle, foreshortening by overlap
sources.bridgman: Constructive Anatomy (1920, public domain): masses before lines, wedging and interlocking of forms, action and inaction sides, the knee as a beveled square
sources.vanderpoel: The Human Figure (1907, public domain): planes before detail, the long axis of each form, the figure as a whole
sources.marvel: How to Draw Comics the Marvel Way (1978): stick figure, then cylinders and boxes, then the contour, then detail; exaggerate the gesture, not the joints
sources.easydrawingguides: easydrawingguides.com superhero tutorials (shared by Evan): a contour-first step order for beginners (head, neck V, shoulders, arms in overlapping curves, torso, legs and kneecap, then costume). We keep its order of parts and its overlapping curves, but construct the forms first so the result works in 3D

steps.name: Line of action
steps.rule: Draw the gesture first. One curve runs head to the weight-bearing foot. Shoulder line and hip line tilt opposite ways (6 to 12 degrees each at rest); the standing ankle sits under the pit of the neck.
steps.model: Pose the armature on this curve before any mesh: spine, then shoulder and hip tilts.

steps.name: Head
steps.rule: A ball for the cranium with its sides sliced flat; the jaw hangs off the front as a wedge down to the chin. Eye line halfway (see the head sheet).

steps.name: Ribcage
steps.rule: Egg-shaped, narrow at the top, widest at the chest line. Tilts back about 10 degrees in side view. Rigid: it moves as one block.

steps.name: Pelvis
steps.form: bowl, or a box narrower at the bottom
steps.rule: Tilts forward (front edge down) about 10 degrees on a man, 15 on a woman. Rigid, and tilts against the ribcage.

steps.name: Waist link
steps.rule: The soft link between the two rigid blocks: bending and twisting happen here. Its front plane is the belly, its back the lumbar hollow.

steps.name: Neck
steps.rule: Leans forward about 15 degrees; rises from the back of the ribcage, not its top. The two neck straps make a V into the pit.

steps.name: Shoulder girdle
steps.rule: Collarbones run from the pit out to the shoulder points in a shallow S; the shoulder blades sit behind. It rides on the ribcage and moves with the arm.

steps.name: Upper arm
steps.rule: The deltoid is a wedge driven into the outer side of the arm; it ends halfway down. The arm hangs slightly back of the body's midline in side view.

steps.name: Elbow
steps.rule: Where planes change, not where wrinkles go. The forearm angles out 5 to 15 degrees from the upper arm (the carrying angle; more on a woman).

steps.name: Forearm
steps.form: tapered cylinder turning into a box

section.shape: round at the elbow, flat box at the wrist

steps.rule: Wide and round near the elbow, flat and box-like at the wrist. Muscle bellies sit in the top half; the bottom half is tendon and narrows.

steps.name: Hand
steps.rule: Block the palm as a flat box, then the fingers as one mitten, then split them (see the hand sheet). The thumb hangs off the side, not the end.

steps.name: Thigh

bulges.what: front of the thigh bows forward

steps.rule: Angles in from the wide hips to the close knees. The front is a long curve, the back flatter.

steps.name: Knee
steps.rule: A beveled square between two cylinders (Bridgman), the kneecap on its front, its bottom halfway from the hip point to the floor.

steps.name: Lower leg

section.shape: D: flat front (the shin bone), round back

steps.rule: Shin front straight, calf back curved: straight against curve. Drops nearly vertical.

steps.name: Foot

section.shape: wedge, high at the instep, low at the toes

steps.rule: Heel block behind, arch on the inside, outer edge flat on the ground. The ankle sits about a quarter of the foot from the heel; the inner ankle bone is higher than the outer.

steps.name: Contour
steps.rule: Only now draw the outline, from form to form. Straight against curve on every limb; bulge peaks offset per step; the nearer form overlaps the farther one at each joint.

steps.name: Planes, then detail
steps.rule: Make the planes read (6 to 8 round a limb) before any detail. Folds and creases only where bone is near the surface: collarbone, elbow, wrist, kneecap, shin, ankles. Bare limbs get no cloth-style wrinkles.

limb_rules: Never put the bulge on both edges of a limb at the same height. That is the sausage limb.
Each limb has an action side (curved) and an inaction side (straighter); they swap from one segment to the next (Bridgman).
Muscle bellies sit near the top of a limb segment; tendons make the lower part narrow (forearm, calf).
Joints are boxes, bellies are cylinders: elbow, knee, wrist and ankle are where the planes change.
In foreshortening, the nearer form overlaps the farther one, and its end ellipse is rounder and bigger.

proportion_systems.use: head 3% bigger, hands and feet 10% bigger

proportion_systems.use: fashion and illustration; looks a little tall in a game

proportion_systems.use: heroes; extra length in the legs, shoulders 2.33 heads

proportion_systems.name: Comic hero (Marvel Way)
proportion_systems.use: superheroes; gesture exaggerated, joints kept true

midjourney.add: anatomically correct adult proportions, relaxed contrapposto, weight on one leg, smooth clean limbs with simple planes, defined knees elbows and ankles, straight shins, full body, front side and back views
midjourney.no: wrinkles, rubber hose arms, sausage limbs, tube limbs, extra fingers, distorted hands
midjourney.why: Midjourney draws limbs as contours; naming the construction qualities (planes, defined joints, straight shins) and banning the failure modes keeps arms and legs clean.
